newsitem.title: USA: Judge rules on counsel in SAFE suit.
newsitem.headline: Judge rules on counsel in SAFE suit.

text.p: A judge has ruled that Cuyahoga County prosecutors will not represent the county in its lawsuit against brokerage houses over a failed investment fund called "SAFE."
Prosecutors and a private law firm for the county could not immediately be reached.
Kenneth Bravo, who represents one of the brokerages, Dean Witter Discover & Co, said Monday the civil suit will go forward with the county represented by its private lawyers.
The "Secured Assets Fund Earnings" fund, or SAFE, a county treasurer's investment program for the county and other local governments, collapsed in 1994 amid rising interest rates.
SAFE, which had more than $1 billion in assets, lost about $114 million when it was shut down after revelations of large paper losses, risky investment strategies and leveraging.

The county in 1995 sued Dean Witter, McDonald & Co Investments Inc, National City Corp, PaineWebber Group Inc, Kemper Scurities (now EVEREN Capital Corp, Travelers Group Inc's Smith Barney Inc and Tucker Anthony Inc.
The suit alleges negligence and violations of fiduciary duties and seeks unspecified compensatory and punitive damages.
Defendants contended the prosecutor's office should not represent the county in the suit, saying at least one member of the prosecutor's staff will be a witness in it.

In a ruling which Bravo said he received over the weekend, visiting County Common Pleas Judge Joseph Grigsby agreed. He said the chief of the prosecutor's civil division countersigned many SAFE contracts and will be called to testify.
